title: The Interaction Algorithm and Practical Fourier Analysis
version: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society B 20(2), July 1958, pp. 361–372, doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1958.tb00300.x.
lineage: Publisher metadata and original summary were previously inspected. The original printed passages in pp. 361–372 were inspected through the browser index of Oxford Academic’s PDF. Stable article landing page links to the publisher PDF; text notes retain the passages and locators.

passages.note: The July 1958 issue contains Good’s analysis of factorial interactions and shortcuts for Fourier analysis.
Generalises the Yates-style factorial-interaction calculation by factoring a direct product of matrices into successive operations on one dimension at a time.

Applies the dimension-by-dimension calculation to multidimensional discrete Fourier transforms. For the one-dimensional transform, §12 uses mutually prime factors and Chinese-remainder index mappings to convert the calculation to a multidimensional transform. It attributes the reverse identification to Good’s 1951 paper and works the 24 = 3 × 8 index example.
passages.quote: the solution of the Chinese remainder problem

passages.note: Further factors composite moduli of the multidimensional discrete Fourier transform when the factors within each modulus are mutually prime.
